newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian wool market eases this week.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian wool market eases this week.

text.p: Australian wool prices eased one percent on average under the weight of an offering in excess of 100,000 bales at sales in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle, the Australian Council of Wool Exporters said in its market report.

Pastoral group Wesfarmers Dalgety Ltd said with the national offering 16 percent larger than originally scheduled last week, general market weakness was expected. It could have been more severe but for the coming Easter break, forcing buyers to cover orders during this period, Wesfarmers said.
The eastern market indicator fell 7.0 cents to 619 cents a kg clean and the western indicator fell 5.0 cents to 589 cents.
A total of 112,236 bales were offered with a pass-in rate of 11.6 percent, the council said. Trade competition was dominated by Japanese, Chinese and Taiwanese interests.
"Exporters felt that the market held up quite well considering the amount of wool on offer which represented an increase of more than 40 percent over the previous week's offering," the council said.
Wesfarmers said the majority of weakness was in the broader end of the market, with prices for 23 micron wools falling by 18 cents in Sydney in the week.
Good prices were paid for stylish fine wools. However, these were limited in selection with many fine wool clips high in vegetable matter and therefore in less demand, Wesfarmers said.

In the futures market, a total of 165 contracts were traded in the 21 micron contract for the week ending 20 March. Open interest increased by 8 contracts to close at 848. The April 1997 contract fell three cents to 725 cents/kg clean.
The Wool International stockpile totalled 1,821,410 bales.
There will be a two week break in auction sales over Easter. Sales resume in the week commencing April 7 in Sydney, Melbourne and Fremantle, with 109,475 bales rostered for sale.
